title: Atom Computing Says It Secures $100 Million To Build Fault-tolerant Quantum Computers
excerpt: Atom Computing secures a $100 million award from the U.S. Department of Commerce to advance development of fault-tolerant quantum computers.
content:
Atom Computing will receive up to $100 million from the U.S. Department of Commerce to accelerate the development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers. The research and development award follows a Letter of Intent from earlier this year and aims to strengthen U.S. leadership in quantum technology. “Quantum computing is reaching a critical inflection point where scientific breakthroughs must rapidly translate into commercial reality,” said Dr. Ben Bloom, CEO and Founder of Atom Computing, explaining that the funding will increase engineering efforts to bring fault-tolerant quantum computing to market.

$100 Million Award Fuels Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer Development

Atom Computing will dedicate the incoming funds to vertically integrating critical technologies and accelerating improvements to system performance and reliability. The company’s neutral-atom architecture is gaining recognition as a promising path toward large-scale quantum computers suitable for commercial applications, a position reinforced by its recent advancement to Stage C of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, with potential funding reaching $300 million.

This DARPA selection highlights the growing confidence in Atom Computing’s approach and its potential to deliver a quantum advantage. The $100 million contract from the U.S. Department of Commerce will also support expansion of Atom Computing’s parallel engineering and testbed infrastructure, intended to rapidly validate innovations and expedite product development, shortening the timeline to economically viable quantum computing.

In 2025, Atom Computing achieved a milestone by selling its first commercial on-premises quantum computer to QuNorth, a Nordic quantum initiative funded by EIFO and Novo Nordisk Foundation, demonstrating early market traction. The company’s strategic research and development initiatives will also focus on strengthening collaboration with supply chain partners to support manufacturing scale-up and long-term growth, positioning it to meet increasing industry and government demand for practical quantum computing solutions.
